high_finding_exact: The English sentence is exact against the Lean: 'where relations of being affected close, read across all steps, whatever bears the costs of its course lies within what can, at some remove, affect its own going on, and whether and when those costs come back to it in time is part of the dynamics (07 §4.11)'.

`MutuallyDependent` puts every formation within every center's `WithinInfluence`. That is the closure of `AffectedBy g h`, under which h exchanges with a condition g depends on. In `LatePair.mutuallyDependent` it runs from `WithinClosure.of_rel (affected : AffectedBy true false)`, so the closure holds what can affect the center at some remove.
'Read across all steps' names what `AffectedBy` collects: dependence at some step and exchange at some step, unordered.
The last clause carries `LatePair`. That pair is mutually dependent while nothing affects anything in time (`not_affectsBefore`) and is mutually dependent in time from no step (`apart`).
'Whatever bears the costs … lies within' is better than astra's 'costs … can return', because the closure holds formations, not costs.
The clause is astra's own proposed fix, 'whether and when they return is part of the dynamics'.
The Chinese also says the limit outright (但这并不保证影响按时间顺序传回来), which is astra's Chinese line.
